title: release.yml artifact names embed run_attempt, so partial re-run always fails the evidence job
description:
release.yml names every qualification artifact with ${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}, so a PARTIAL re-run can never resolve artifacts produced by an earlier attempt. `gh run rerun --failed` is therefore structurally unusable on this workflow.

MEASURED on run 34801853367 (v0.6.2 qualification), not inferred:
  attempt 1 produced  ladybug-benchmark-qualification-linux-x64-34801853367-1
                      ladybug-concurrency-qualification-34801853367-1
  attempt 2 produced  ladybug-package-qualification-<platform>-34801853367-2
  and the evidence job on attempt 2 failed with:
      Unable to download artifact(s): Artifact not found for name:
      ladybug-benchmark-qualification-linux-x64-34801853367-2

The producing jobs succeeded on attempt 1, so --failed correctly did not re-run them; their artifacts keep the -1 suffix while the consumer on attempt 2 looks only for -2. Nothing is wrong with either job. The naming makes them unable to meet.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A CURIOSITY: the Ladybug concurrency job is genuinely flaky -- on this same run it timed out after 5000ms on "Ladybug projection lifecycle > builds, verifies, reuses, disposes, and deterministically rebuilds one immutable generation", then passed on re-run, having succeeded on both prior release dispatches. A flaky job in a release workflow is precisely where an operator reaches for `gh run rerun --failed`, and on this workflow that will ALWAYS fail in the evidence job, in a way that looks like a second, unrelated defect. The workaround is a full `gh run rerun`, which re-runs every job including the expensive ones.

SHAPE OF A FIX, not prescribed: either drop run_attempt from the artifact names (run_id alone is unique per run, and upload-artifact v4 refuses duplicate names within a run, which is presumably why the attempt suffix was added), or have the consumer resolve the newest matching artifact rather than an exact name, or make the evidence job depend on artifacts in a way that tolerates an earlier attempt. Whoever takes it should check what upload-artifact v4 actually does on a partial re-run before choosing.

Found during the v0.6.2 release, 2026-09-13. Did not block that release -- a full re-run was used instead.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `gh run rerun --failed` on release.yml completes, with the evidence job resolving artifacts produced by an earlier attempt rather than failing on an exact-name miss
The chosen fix is proven against a real partial re-run, not just reasoned about -- a release-workflow dispatch where one job is re-run and the evidence job still assembles
Whichever way it is fixed, a comment records WHY run_attempt was in the name, so the next person does not reintroduce it to solve the duplicate-name problem it was presumably there for
The Ladybug concurrency flake is separately recorded or linked, since the value of fixing partial re-run depends on a flake existing to re-run around

implementationNotes:
INVESTIGATION ONLY, 2026-09-14 — no code changed, task returned to To Do so LCLI-490 could
take priority (orchestrator's call: the e2e harness's possibly-inert assertions sit UNDERNEATH
a required check, whereas this only bites on a partial re-run of a release dispatch and no
release is pending). Recording what was established so none of it is re-derived.

MEASURED, not reasoned about:

1. ARTIFACTS ARE RUN-SCOPED, AND A FULL RE-RUN DELETES THE EARLIER ATTEMPTS'. Run 34801853367
   is at run_attempt=3, and the artifacts API now lists ONLY the -3 names. Attempts 1 and 2
   provably produced -1 and -2 artifacts (this task's own description records their names and
   the failure they caused), and those are gone. So a FULL re-run clears the slate; only a
   PARTIAL re-run leaves an earlier attempt's artifacts alongside a new one.

2. THAT IS WHY THE ATTEMPT SUFFIX EXISTS, and AC#3 asks for this to be written down: with a
   stable name, a partial re-run's upload would collide with the surviving artifact from the
   earlier attempt, and upload-artifact v4 FAILS on a duplicate name within a run. The suffix
   buys collision-freedom and pays for it with consumers that cannot find a non-re-run
   producer's output. Do not simply delete the suffix -- that trades a consumer failure for a
   producer failure, which is not obviously better.

3. THE LIKELY FIX IS `overwrite: true` ON THE UPLOADS PLUS STABLE NAMES. upload-artifact
   exposes an `overwrite` input ("an artifact with a matching name will be deleted before a
   new one is uploaded... Does not fail if the artifact does not exist"). NOT YET CONFIRMED AT
   THE PINNED SHA ea165f8d (v4.6.2) -- I read it from the action's default branch, and an
   attempt to read action.yml at that exact ref failed on the gh invocation, so this is the
   one load-bearing fact still unverified. Confirm it at the pin before building on it.

4. MIXING ATTEMPTS WITHIN A RUN IS SAFE, which is what makes stable names acceptable. Every
   artifact in a run comes from the same head_sha, and release.yml's package job already
   asserts `report.repository.commit === GITHUB_SHA` for each platform report. So consuming an
   attempt-1 package report alongside an attempt-2 concurrency report cannot silently mix
   commits. That invariant is the reason a "newest matching artifact" scheme is not needed.

5. REJECTED: having the consumer pattern-match across attempts. `download-artifact` with
   `pattern:` + `merge-multiple: true` would pull EVERY attempt's copy into one directory,
   with no ordering guarantee about which wins. For a qualification gate that is worse than
   the current hard failure.

6. A SECOND, LATENT INSTANCE IS ALREADY IN THE FILE. `npm-packages` (release.yml ~line 565)
   is uploaded with NO attempt suffix, so on a partial re-run where the package job re-runs it
   would hit exactly the duplicate-name failure described in (2). It has not bitten because
   the package job has not yet been partially re-run. Whatever fix is chosen must cover it.

7. CROSS-FILE COUPLING THAT WILL BREAK IF THE NAMES CHANGE — check this before touching
   release.yml. scripts/publish-release.sh (LCLI-489) downloads the qualification reports with
   `-p "ladybug-package-qualification-*-${RUN_ID}-${attempt}"` and resolves the attempt from
   the API, with a RUN_ATTEMPT override. Dropping the suffix makes that pattern match nothing
   and makes RUN_ATTEMPT meaningless. The two changes must land together, and
   test/publish-release-script.test.ts asserts on the attempt-suffixed directory names, so it
   changes too.

AC#2 IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE and shapes how this should be scheduled: it requires proving the fix
against a REAL partial re-run, which means a release-workflow dispatch plus a deliberately
failed job to re-run. Budget a full dispatch cycle for it, and do not claim it from reasoning.

RESOLVED, 2026-09-14: the one load-bearing fact the earlier note left unverified.

`overwrite` DOES exist as an input at the PINNED sha ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
(actions/upload-artifact v4.6.2 — and that sha is what the v4.6.2 tag resolves to, checked).
Read from action.yml at that exact ref, not from the action's default branch, because the
earlier note explicitly flagged that distinction as the thing not yet established. Its
documented behaviour, verbatim:

    If true, an artifact with a matching name will be deleted before a new one is uploaded.
    If false, the action will fail if an artifact for the given name already exists.
    Does not fail if the artifact does not exist.
    default: 'false'

The full input list at that sha: name, path, if-no-files-found, retention-days,
compression-level, overwrite, include-hidden-files.

So the proposed fix — stable artifact names plus `overwrite: true` — is buildable on the
version already pinned, with NO action bump required. "Does not fail if the artifact does not
exist" is the clause that makes it safe on a first attempt as well as a re-run.

WHAT IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is now the only thing standing between this and a
change: AC#2's real partial re-run. Everything above is about what the ACTION does; nothing
here proves what GITHUB does to a prior attempt's artifacts during `gh run rerun --failed`
specifically. The measured evidence (run 34801853367, attempt 3, only -3 artifacts surviving)
came from a FULL re-run, which is a different operation. The task description's own record of
attempt 2 failing to find a -2 artifact while -1 artifacts existed is the only direct evidence
about the partial case, and it is second-hand within this repo rather than re-measured.
Budget a dispatch for it and do not claim it from reasoning.

=== 2. THE DISPATCH THAT FAULT EXISTS FOR ===

Release run 34888537835, dispatched on this branch, publish=false so it is a DRY RUN and

               package-qualification and the evidence job are skipped by the needs graph.
  then      -- `gh run rerun --failed 34888537835`
  attempt 2 -- concurrency + package-qualification + evidence re-run. ladybug-qualification
               (the benchmark job) does NOT re-run, so the evidence job must resolve
               ladybug-benchmark-qualification-linux-x64-34888537835 produced on ATTEMPT 1.
               That resolution is the whole point: it is precisely what failed on run
               34801853367 and what this task exists to fix.

IF THE EVIDENCE JOB ASSEMBLES ON ATTEMPT 2, AC#2 IS SATISFIED and can be checked. If it does
not, the fix is wrong and the revert is mechanical: put `-${{ github.run_attempt }}` back on

- Artifacts are run-scoped and a FULL re-run deletes earlier attempts' artifacts; only a

comments.body:
THE TRANSFERABLE FORM OF THIS DEFECT, which is worth more than the workflow-specific write-up in the description:

**An artifact name that embeds the attempt number silently couples every consumer to the same attempt as its producer.**

That coupling is invisible in normal operation -- every job runs on the same attempt, every name agrees, nothing is wrong. It becomes visible only when someone re-runs a SUBSET, which is exactly the moment a release is already going badly and the operator is reaching for the fastest recovery available. So the failure mode is reserved for the worst time to meet it, and it presents as a second, unrelated-looking defect on top of the first.

It also punishes the correct instinct. `gh run rerun --failed` is the right reflex: it is faster, it does not repeat expensive jobs, and it is what the tooling advertises for a partial failure. Here it is the one option that can never work, and nothing in the error message says so -- the evidence job simply reports an artifact not found, which reads as a missing upload rather than an attempt mismatch.

Generalisation contributed by opum-agent while reviewing the finding; recorded because the description above explains THIS workflow and this sentence explains the class. Anyone naming an artifact should ask whether a consumer could ever run on a different attempt than the producer. If yes, the attempt number does not belong in the name.
